positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Working on a new version of the Virtual Agent located at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/contact/virtual-agent/.  The site uses C#, .NET Core, and Bot Framework on the back-end and React, Redux, and TypeScript on the front-end.

positions.title: Contract Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software Engineer working on contract with Microsoft through TEKsystems.  Primarily responsible for working with a team to develop a new front end and back end for the Microsoft Virtual Agent.  
The Virtual Agent is a chatbot that helps users with Microsoft related questions and connects them with a human agent if it fails to solve the user’s issue
Site: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/contact/virtual-agent/
React, Redux, and TypeScript have been used for the client side.
Jest and Enzyme used for client side unit tests.
The server side uses C#, ASP.Net Core, and the Microsoft Bot Framework to facilitate messages between the client and a service providing an intelligent response to a query.
LUIS utilized to understand the intent of a message coming from the client.
MSTest used for server side unit tests.
The Virtual Agent is hosted using Microsoft Azure.
Worked on a hackathon project to connect the Google Assistant to the Virtual Agent.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Created a web tool for Corteva to track customer seed sales, licenses and generate remittances.
Wrote an uploader tool to carry out CRUD operations as well as validate Excel data.
Built a domain service that generated PDFs of remittances based on customer data input.
Generated service proxies from API endpoints using NSwag.
Ran migrations to make database changes via code first Entity Framework.
Use asynchronous programming in C# backend to ensure good front end responsiveness.
Unit tested the API portion of the web tool using xUnit and Shouldly.
Worked on a legacy WebForms tool for Corteva that allowed for seed sale forecasting.
Developed a C# console application that kept databases for the new and legacy tool in sync.
Extensive SQL use for manual backend database manipulation.
Followed strict company Git practices.
